text: Mister Utterson was sitting by his fireside. <break time="0.8s" /> One evening after dinner. <break time="0.8s" /> When he was surprised to receive a visit. <break time="0.8s" /> From Poole, Doctor Jekylls butler. <break time="0.8s" /> The butler. <break time="0.8s" /> Who was usually calm and proper. <break time="0.8s" /> Now looked so pale and nervous. <break time="0.8s" /> That Utterson asked him. <break time="0.8s" /> Whether the doctor was ill. <break time="0.8s" /> I have been afraid for about a week. <break time="0.8s" /> Poole said. <break time="0.8s" /> And I can bear it no more. <break time="0.8s" /> For I think there has been foul play. <break time="0.8s" /> Poole would not explain any further. <break time="0.8s" /> But he begged the lawyer. <break time="0.8s" /> To come with him at once. <break time="0.8s" /> And see the matter for himself. <break time="0.8s" /> Utterson rose without another word. <break time="0.8s" /> And the two men went out together. <break time="0.8s" /> Into the wild, cold March night. <break time="0.8s" /> Under a pale moon. <break time="0.8s" /> The wind made talking difficult. <break time="0.8s" /> And it seemed to have swept the streets. <break time="0.8s" /> Unusually bare of people. <break time="0.8s" /> That night. <break time="0.8s" /> Never had Utterson felt. <break time="0.8s" /> So sharp a wish. <break time="0.8s" /> To see and touch his fellow human beings. <break time="0.8s" /> For a heavy fear. <break time="0.8s" /> Was pressing on his mind. <break time="0.8s" /> When they reached the square. <break time="0.8s" /> Poole stopped and wiped his brow. <break time="0.8s" /> With a red handkerchief. <break time="0.8s" /> But it was fear, not the hurry. <break time="0.8s" /> That had made him sweat. <break time="0.8s" /> Well, sir, here we are he said. <break time="0.8s" /> And God grant that there be nothing wrong.
